key_insight: Neural networks discover strongly nonlinear water-wave candidates with near-machine-precision equation residuals, while interval arithmetic and Lean independently certify a residual bound for one candidate.
engineering_relevance: The framework shows how learned PDE solutions can gain auditable numerical guarantees rather than relying solely on sampled residuals.
method: Train physics-informed neural networks without training data to learn wave profiles, speeds and continuation parameters.
Freeze one candidate into a finite representation and bound its residual using interval arithmetic, including roundoff, truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors.
Use Lean to machine-check the deductions from certified numerical bounds to the residual theorem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery of Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples, new high-amplitude candidates through continuation, and rigorous residual certification of one candidate.
watch_item: A certified small residual is not by itself a proof of existence, uniqueness or stability of a nearby exact wave.
paper_title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
